# 1 Clement Chapter 26 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** Codex Alexandrinus, 1 Clement 26 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/1CL_026_page_001.jpg

---

## Chapter 26

**26:1** Shall we then think it a great and wonderful thing if the Creator of all things raises up those who have served him in holiness and in the assurance of good faith, when even through a bird he shows us the greatness of his promise?

**26:2** For it says somewhere: "You shall raise me up and I will give you thanks;" and: "I lay down and slept, and I arose, for you are with me."

**26:3** And again Job says: "You shall raise up this flesh of mine, which has endured all these things."

---

## Translator's Note

Chapter 26 is the conclusion of Clement's phoenix argument. The rhetorical question in v. 1 is a classic *a fortiori*: if God works resurrection in nature (through the phoenix), how much more certainly will he raise his own faithful servants? The two psalm citations in v. 2 appear to be from Psalm 28:7 (LXX) and Psalm 3:5 (LXX). The Job citation in v. 3 echoes Job 19:26 (LXX), the famous resurrection text. The formula "it says somewhere" (*pou*) reflects a loose citation method common in early Christian literature (cf. Hebrews 2:6, 4:4).

---

*SOPHIA represents the consensus translation, balancing literalness and clarity.*
